A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HOI-PAGE. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial rewriting and reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original generation experiments, quantitative comparisons, ablations, and a 30-participant perceptual study, with additional qualitative results in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds foundation-model robustness experiments, part-contact measurements, quantitative BEHAVE comparisons, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The PAG construction, segmentation, reference-video generation, alignment, and object-motion optimization procedures remain substantively unchanged. The appendix prompts also match; the new planning and grounding terminology reframes existing stages, while alternative foundation models are tested as experimental variants.

E1.justification: Both versions use Sketchfab objects and BEHAVE scans and demonstrate single-person, multi-person, single-object, and multi-object interactions. BEHAVE already appears in v1 Appendix A; v2 expands its evaluation without introducing a new dataset, domain, or interaction family.

E2.justification: HOI-Diff and CHOIS remain the Sketchfab comparators. V2 additionally evaluates them on the retained BEHAVE benchmark in Table 6 and Figure 11, where v1 showed only HOI-PAGE examples, providing a bounded extension of comparator participation.

E3.justification: V2 adds part-contact evaluation using manually verified LLM-identified relations and distance thresholds of 1, 3, and 5 cm. It also specifies a quantitative BEHAVE protocol with 18 test objects, three prompts per object, and five variations per prompt, and adds Gemini and HunyuanVideo substitution experiments; the original main evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained fitting, contact, and motion-state ablations, v2 adds foundation-model sensitivity tests in Table 4, fine-grained contact analysis, a pipeline-stage case study in Figure 10, and runtime profiling in Table 7. These substantially broaden examination of component dependence, contact fidelity, and computational cost.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and perceptual-study percentages without confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The added experiments introduce no new uncertainty-estimation practice; BEHAVE's five generated variations follow the existing diversity-sampling approach.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the perceptual-study values remain unchanged, but Tables 4–7 add substantial results. For example, Table 5 reports 1 cm contact accuracy of 0.887 for HOI-PAGE versus 0.318 for HOI-Diff and 0.274 for CHOIS; Table 6 newly reports BEHAVE VideoCLIP scores of 0.220, 0.200, and 0.214, respectively. These are additional evaluations, not improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Appendix A newly defines thresholded part-contact accuracy and contact distance averaged from minimum part distances across frames. The PAG definitions and optimization mathematics otherwise remain equivalent; condensed fitting-loss notation and renumbered equations introduce no new proof or theoretical guarantee.

C1.justification: Both versions claim zero-shot 4D interaction generation through LLM-derived part affordances, improved realism and text alignment, and flexibility across multiple people or objects. V2's emphasis on explicit planning and interaction scaffolding preserves the meaning and scope of these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new substitutions as evidence of robustness across foundation models and explicitly adds degenerate segmentation to potential failure sources. Appendix B newly characterizes the pipeline as unoptimized but practical for offline synthesis and discusses possible acceleration; the finger-articulation limitation remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds stagewise runtimes of 0.6, 5.7, 8.3, and 6.0 minutes in Table 7, extending v1's optimization-only timing disclosure. The hardware, iteration counts, alignment procedure, and full prompts are retained, while v1's explicit promise to release code and data upon publication is omitted.

R1.justification: V2 adds HIMO, TOUCH, and OpenHOI, acknowledging supervised multi-object and complementary hand-object synthesis research. It also elaborates the contrast with ZeroHOI, while retaining the broader positioning around zero-shot generation with explicit part-level structure.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method undergo extensive rewriting around interaction planning and grounding, with renamed and regrouped subsections and condensed mathematical exposition. The appendix is reorganized, author information and citation style change, and impact and writing-assistance disclosures are added.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the pipeline diagram, adds the intermediate-results visualization and Tables 4–7, and expands the BEHAVE illustration into a baseline comparison. Existing figures and tables are relocated or rearranged, and the appendix changes from two-column to full-width presentation alongside a new document layout.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central part-affordance claim: v1 measured contact globally and demonstrated BEHAVE only qualitatively, whereas v2 adds manually verified part-contact evaluation and quantitative BEHAVE baseline comparisons. Foundation-model sensitivity tests, intermediate outputs, and runtime profiling further clarify dependencies and practical costs. Uncertainty reporting remains limited, but the new evidence addresses important experimental gaps and supports a substantial overall improvement.
